title: Private Observability Minimum Pack — Dashboard Catalog
author: Sergio Costa
body:
## Overview
This page is the canonical catalog of Grafana dashboards shipped in the **Private Observability Minimum Pack** ("min pack") for **Redwood Private** deployments (VPC and on‑prem, including air‑gapped).

The goal of the catalog is to:
- Define what dashboards are included by default and what each is used for.
- Specify required signals (metrics/logs) per dashboard so operators can validate “supported” status.
- Provide links/pointers to **canonical panels/queries** so teams don’t fork ad‑hoc dashboards.

**Pack versioning note:** dashboard provisioning is versioned with the min pack bundle (e.g., `observability-pack v0.x`). A Private install pins a bundle version via the installer/Helm values. For details, see the install guide.

---

## Conventions used in this catalog
### Dashboard naming + foldering
Dashboards are provisioned into the Grafana folder:
- **`Redwood Private / Minimum Pack`**

Dashboard titles follow:
- `Private / <Area> / <Dashboard Name>`

### Standard Grafana templating variables
All dashboards should expose (where applicable):
- `cluster` (or `environment`) 
- `namespace`
- `tenant` (may be `all` in single-tenant installs)
- `route`
- `model`
- `instance` / `pod`
- `region` (VPC) 

### Metric + label expectations
This catalog assumes the metrics/labels in:
- **Private observability minimum signals standard** (see related pages)

If a metric exists but labels are missing (e.g., `model`), the dashboard may render but will not be considered “supported” for go‑live until fixed.

### Logging expectations
Where dashboards reference logs, the pack assumes structured JSON logs emitted by:
- `gateway`
- `runtime`
- `control-plane` services

and collected by the supported log forwarder (Vector/Fluent Bit) into the customer’s backend.

---

## Dashboard inventory (summary)
| Dashboard | Primary audience | Purpose | Key dependencies |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Private / Gateway / Service Overview** | Operators, on-call, support | Golden signals at the API edge: traffic, latency, errors, disconnects | Gateway HTTP metrics + structured gateway logs |
| **Private / Runtime / Performance** | Operators, performance on-call | Prefill/decode latency, queueing, batching, cache effectiveness | Runtime metrics (prefill/decode, queue depth, batch size, KV cache) |
| **Private / Runtime / GPU Saturation** | Operators, infra/SRE | GPU utilization/memory/throttling correlated with latency/errors | DCGM/NVIDIA exporter metrics + runtime latency |
| **Private / Routing / Fallbacks** | Operators, platform, support | Model routing outcomes, fallbacks, retry behavior, policy errors | Gateway/router metrics + control-plane policy metrics |
| **Private / Control Plane / Health** | Operators, platform | Control plane availability and correctness (auth/policy/config) | Control plane service metrics + error logs |
| **Private / Installer & Upgrade / Install Health** | Operators, solutions, release eng | Installer controller health, upgrades/rollbacks, provisioning success | Installer health metrics + Kubernetes events |
| **Private / Logging / Pipeline Health** | Operators, security ops | Detect log drops/backpressure/export failures and missing signals | Collector/exporter metrics + collector logs |
| **Private / Prometheus & Rules / Monitoring Health** | Operators, SRE | Detect scrape failures, rule evaluation errors, missing targets | Prometheus self-metrics + rule metrics |

---

## Dashboard details

### 1) Private / Gateway / Service Overview
**Audience:** On-call (first responder), operators, Support

**When to use:**
- “Is the API up?” and “What’s broken?”
- Triaging elevated latency, 5xx spikes, or streaming disconnects

**Core panels (canonical):**
- RPS (by `route`, optional by `tenant`)
- Error rate (4xx vs 5xx)
- Latency p50/p95/p99 (request + time-to-first-token where applicable)
- In-flight requests / concurrency
- Streaming disconnects / client cancellations
- Top error codes (requires structured logs and/or error label mapping)

**Required metrics (minimum):**
- `redwood_gateway_requests_total{route,method,status_class,tenant,model}`
- `redwood_gateway_request_duration_seconds_bucket{route,tenant,model}`
- `redwood_gateway_stream_disconnects_total{route,tenant,model,reason}`
- `redwood_gateway_inflight_requests{route}`

**Recommended logs (for drill-down links):**
- Gateway access logs with fields: `request_id`, `tenant_id`, `route`, `model`, `status`, `latency_ms`, `error_code`, `streaming`, `bytes_out`, `user_agent`

**Canonical PromQL snippets:**
- RPS (5m):
  - `sum by (route) (rate(redwood_gateway_requests_total{status_class!="5xx"}[5m]))`
- 5xx rate (5m):
  - `sum(rate(redwood_gateway_requests_total{status_class="5xx"}[5m])) / sum(rate(redwood_gateway_requests_total[5m]))`
- p95 latency (5m):
  - `histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, route) (rate(redwood_gateway_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])))`

**Notes / gotchas:**
- If `model` is missing from gateway metrics, model-specific panels must be hidden or will aggregate incorrectly.
- For multi-tenant installs, operators should default the `tenant` variable to “all” and only filter when investigating.

---

### 2) Private / Runtime / Performance
**Audience:** Performance on-call, operators, platform runtime engineers

**When to use:**
- Latency regression investigation (prefill vs decode)
- Queue buildup, throughput collapse, poor batching or cache hit rate

**Core panels (canonical):**
- Prefill latency p50/p95/p99
- Decode latency per token p50/p95/p99
- Tokens/s (emitted and/or processed)
- Queue depth and time in queue
- Batch size distribution (continuous batching)
- KV cache hit ratio (prefix/KV cache effectiveness)
- OOM / runtime errors (count + rate)

**Required metrics (minimum):**
- `redwood_runtime_prefill_duration_seconds_bucket{model,tenant}`
- `redwood_runtime_decode_token_duration_seconds_bucket{model,tenant}`
- `redwood_runtime_tokens_emitted_total{model,tenant}`
- `redwood_runtime_queue_depth{model}`
- `redwood_runtime_queue_wait_seconds_bucket{model}`
- `redwood_runtime_batch_size_bucket{model}`
- `redwood_runtime_kv_cache_hit_ratio{model}`
- `redwood_runtime_errors_total{model,error_code}`

**Canonical PromQL snippets:**
- Prefill p99 (5m):
  - `histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le, model) (rate(redwood_runtime_prefill_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])))`
- Decode per-token p95 (5m):
  - `histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, model) (rate(redwood_runtime_decode_token_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])))`
- Queue depth (max over 5m):
  - `max_over_time(redwood_runtime_queue_depth[5m])`
- Tokens/s (5m):
  - `sum by (model) (rate(redwood_runtime_tokens_emitted_total[5m]))`

**Notes / gotchas:**
- Ensure histograms are configured with stable buckets; do not change bucket boundaries without a coordinated pack update.
- If `tenant` is high-cardinality, dashboards should default to `tenant="all"` aggregation and discourage per-tenant breakdown unless explicitly enabled.

---

### 3) Private / Runtime / GPU Saturation
**Audience:** Operators, infra/SRE, solutions engineers

**When to use:**
- Correlating latency/errors with GPU resource constraints
- Detecting throttling, memory pressure, or mis-sized GPU pools

**Core panels (canonical):**
- GPU utilization (%) by node/GPU
- GPU memory used (%) and absolute
- Power / throttling indicators (when available)
- GPU temperature (optional; noisy in some environments)
- Overlay: runtime p95/p99 latency vs GPU utilization

**Required metrics (minimum):**
One of the following sources is required; the min pack supports either:
- **DCGM exporter** (preferred):
  - `DCGM_FI_DEV_GPU_UTIL{gpu,instance}`
  - `DCGM_FI_DEV_FB_USED{gpu,instance}` and `DCGM_FI_DEV_FB_TOTAL{gpu,instance}`
  - `DCGM_FI_DEV_CLOCK_THROTTLE_REASONS{gpu,instance}` (if enabled)
- **nvidia-smi exporter** (fallback, less complete):
  - `nvidia_smi_utilization_gpu{gpu,instance}`
  - `nvidia_smi_memory_used_bytes{gpu,instance}` and `nvidia_smi_memory_total_bytes{gpu,instance}`

Plus runtime latency metrics from **Private / Runtime / Performance** for correlation.

**Canonical PromQL snippets:**
- GPU utilization (avg over 5m):
  - `avg by (instance, gpu) (avg_over_time(DCGM_FI_DEV_GPU_UTIL[5m]))`
- GPU memory used %:
  - `100 * (avg by (instance,gpu)(DCGM_FI_DEV_FB_USED) / avg by (instance,gpu)(DCGM_FI_DEV_FB_TOTAL))`

**Notes / gotchas:**
- Label joins between node exporters and Kubernetes node names vary by customer; this dashboard expects a working `instance` ↔ node mapping in Prometheus.
- If customers run MIG, ensure the chosen exporter exposes stable identifiers that don’t explode cardinality.

---

### 4) Private / Routing / Fallbacks
**Audience:** Operators, platform on-call, support

**When to use:**
- Investigating unexpected model selection, fallback activation, or elevated retry rates
- Diagnosing “wrong model” complaints and capacity-driven degradations

**Core panels (canonical):**
- Request counts by `requested_model` vs `served_model`
- Fallback rate (overall and by route/model)
- Fallback reasons (capacity, policy, compatibility, region)
- Retry rate and retry success rate
- Policy store/config fetch errors (control-plane interaction)

**Required metrics (minimum):**
- `redwood_router_requests_total{route,tenant,requested_model,served_model,outcome}`
- `redwood_router_fallbacks_total{route,tenant,reason}`
- `redwood_router_retries_total{route,reason}`
- `redwood_policy_fetch_errors_total{service}` (or equivalent control-plane metric)

**Recommended logs:**
- Router/gateway decision logs with fields: `request_id`, `route`, `requested_model`, `served_model`, `fallback_reason`, `policy_version`

**Canonical PromQL snippets:**
- Fallback rate (5m):
  - `sum(rate(redwood_router_fallbacks_total[5m])) / sum(rate(redwood_router_requests_total[5m]))`
- Outcome breakdown:
  - `sum by (outcome) (rate(redwood_router_requests_total[5m]))`

**Notes / gotchas:**
- Ensure `requested_model` and `served_model` are bounded enumerations (model versions can be mapped to a stable label) to prevent accidental high-cardinality.

---

### 5) Private / Control Plane / Health
**Audience:** Operators, platform teams

**When to use:**
- Authentication/authorization issues
- Policy/config propagation delays
- Control-plane partial outage impacting routing, quotas, or rollouts

**Core panels (canonical):**
- Control plane API availability (success rate, latency)
- Auth integration health (OIDC/JWKS fetch, token validation errors)
- Policy store / config service health (write/read errors, replication lag if available)
- Rate-limit/quota evaluation errors

**Required metrics (minimum):**
- `redwood_control_plane_requests_total{service,endpoint,status_class}`
- `redwood_control_plane_request_duration_seconds_bucket{service,endpoint}`
- `redwood_auth_token_validation_errors_total{reason}`
- `redwood_config_apply_errors_total{component}`

**Recommended logs:**
- Control-plane audit/event logs (non-sensitive) with fields: `actor`, `action`, `resource_type`, `resource_id`, `status`

**Notes / gotchas:**
- This dashboard must not expose secrets; panels should use counts/rates, not raw payloads.

---

### 6) Private / Installer & Upgrade / Install Health
**Audience:** Operators, Solutions/Pro Services, release engineering

**When to use:**
- Installation or upgrade stuck
- Grafana provisioning failures, rule loading issues, mismatched bundle versions

**Core panels (canonical):**
- Installer controller liveness/readiness
- Current installed versions (Private installer + observability pack bundle)
- Provisioning step durations (download/apply/provision)
- Upgrade/rollback attempts and outcomes
- Kubernetes resource readiness summary (Deployments/DaemonSets for observability components)

**Required metrics (minimum):**
- `redwood_installer_health{component}` (gauge; 1 healthy / 0 unhealthy)
- `redwood_installer_steps_total{step,outcome}`
- `redwood_installer_step_duration_seconds_bucket{step}`
- `redwood_installer_bundle_info{bundle,version}` (info metric)

**Recommended logs:**
- Installer logs with fields: `step`, `bundle_version`, `error_code`, `k8s_resource`

**Canonical PromQL snippets:**
- Step failure rate (15m):
  - `sum(rate(redwood_installer_steps_total{outcome="failure"}[15m]))`
- Slow steps p95 (1h):
  - `histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, step) (rate(redwood_installer_step_duration_seconds_bucket[1h])))`

**Notes / gotchas:**
- This dashboard is the primary source for diagnosing the common failure mode: dashboards provisioned but Prometheus rules not loaded (or vice versa).

---

### 7) Private / Logging / Pipeline Health
**Audience:** Operators, security/IT ops

**When to use:**
- Missing logs in SIEM
- Suspected log drops during high load
- Collector/exporter misconfiguration

**Core panels (canonical):**
- Collector input rate vs output rate
- Buffer/backlog depth (if supported by collector)
- Drop counters and reasons
- Export failures (HTTP status codes, retries)
- “Missing signals” indicators (e.g., gateway logs present but runtime logs absent)

**Required metrics (minimum):**
Depends on collector:
- **Vector**:
  - `vector_events_in_total{component_id}`
  - `vector_events_out_total{component_id}`
  - `vector_component_errors_total{component_id}`
  - `vector_component_sent_events_total{component_id}` (if enabled)
- **Fluent Bit**:
  - `fluentbit_input_bytes_total{input}` / `fluentbit_output_proc_bytes_total{output}`
  - `fluentbit_output_errors_total{output}`

**Recommended logs:**
- Collector logs (warn/error) shipped to the same backend, with `component_id`/plugin identification

**Canonical queries (PromQL examples):**
- Vector drop/error rate:
  - `sum(rate(vector_component_errors_total[5m]))`
- Input vs output (sanity):
  - `sum(rate(vector_events_in_total[5m])) - sum(rate(vector_events_out_total[5m]))`

**Notes / gotchas:**
- Customers often add aggressive filters; this dashboard should make it obvious when filters are dropping required Redwood logs.
- For regulated customers, ensure redaction is configured before forwarding to external SIEM.

---

### 8) Private / Prometheus & Rules / Monitoring Health
**Audience:** Operators, SRE

**When to use:**
- Dashboards show gaps (“No data”)
- Alerts not firing (rule evaluation or loading issues)
- Scrape failures after upgrades

**Core panels (canonical):**
- Target scrape health by job
- Scrape duration and samples ingested
- Rule evaluation failures
- TSDB ingestion pressure (optional; depends on backend)
- Alertmanager notification errors (if Alertmanager is used)

**Required metrics (minimum):**
Prometheus self-metrics (Prometheus-compatible systems should map equivalents):
- `up{job}`
- `scrape_duration_seconds{job}`
- `prometheus_rule_evaluation_failures_total`
- `prometheus_engine_query_duration_seconds_bucket` (optional)

**Canonical PromQL snippets:**
- Scrape down targets:
  - `sum by (job) (1 - up)`
- Rule evaluation failures (5m):
  - `rate(prometheus_rule_evaluation_failures_total[5m])`

**Notes / gotchas:**
- This dashboard is mandatory for troubleshooting “alerts didn’t fire” incidents; check rule load/eval health before tuning thresholds.

---

## Cross-dashboard drill-down links (standard)
Dashboards should link to one another using consistent panel links:
- Gateway 5xx panel → Runtime Performance (filtered by `model`) and Logging Pipeline Health
- Runtime GPU saturation panel → Runtime Performance (same node/GPU scope)
- Routing fallbacks panel → Control Plane Health (policy/config errors) and Gateway Overview

---

## Supportability checklist mapping
A Private install is considered “supported” (observability minimum) when:
- All dashboards load without missing-data errors in the default variable selections.
- The required metrics listed above exist and include required labels.
- Log pipeline health shows no sustained drop/backpressure and required service logs are observable.

Operators should validate using the **Private observability signal validation checklist** (related page) before go-live.

---

## Ownership and change process
**Owner:** Eng Platform → Dashboards & Alerts (DRI: Sergio Costa)

Changes to this catalog or dashboards should be made via:
- PR against `observability-pack` repo (dashboard JSON + provisioning)
- Update this Confluence page in the same release window

For new dashboards, include:
- Required signals and label cardinality review
- “First responder” workflow (what decision does the dashboard enable?)
- Backwards-compat plan for existing Private customers
